Book a demoHow it works

Three layers. Each one on point.

A context layer is only as reliable as its weakest layer, so Atlas is built as three, and each one does a single job well.

  1. 01Structure

    Structure what your company knows.

    Skills, knowledge and metrics, each a typed object with an owner and a scope. Not a pile of documents: a procedure is a skill, a fact is a page, a number is a metric.

    • Skills
    • Knowledge
    • Metrics
    • Scopes
  2. 02Maintain

    Maintain it with people in the loop.

    Every save is a version. Agents propose changes as diffs a person approves. Scheduled workflows keep pages current, and every change lands in the audit log.

    • Versions
    • Change requests
    • Workflows
    • Audit log
  3. 03Retrieve

    Retrieve it from any agent.

    One MCP endpoint. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT or your own agent signs in as a person, searches what that person can open, and reads the same copy as everyone else.

    • MCP
    • Search
    • Tool policy
    • API keys

One copy. Any number of readers.

Skills are how work gets done. Knowledge is what is true. Metrics are what words mean. Each is kept once, in Atlas, and every agent retrieves the same copy.

Everything in each layer, and how it stays honest.

Pick a layer, then an object, to see what it looks like inside Atlas.

01

Skills

How a job is done here. A skill is a written procedure that agents follow. Each save is a new version with a note on what changed, and an owner can restore any older one.

skill · month-end-close · v0.1.4 · published

02

Knowledge

What is true here. Pages your team writes together in a live editor, with comments, tasks and links between pages. Agents read the same pages people do.

page · finance / payout schedule · live

03

Metrics

What a word means here. A metric is SQL over your BigQuery or Snowflake warehouse, agreed once. Tables carry notes on how to use them, and every agent answers from the same definition.

metric · active customers · bigquery · run preview

04

Scopes

Who may see it. Pages and skills sit in a teamspace or in someone's private space, with view, comment, edit or full access. An agent never sees more than the person it works for.

scope · finance › payout schedule › maya chen (edit)

05

Versions

Every save is a new version with who made it. Nothing is overwritten. Open any earlier version, compare it, and restore it as a new one.

v4 › v5 › v6 › v7 (restored v4)

06

Change requests

An agent's edit arrives as a change request. A person reads the diff and approves or rejects it, block by block, like a pull request.

change request · payout schedule · from claude code · pending review

07

Workflows

Scheduled jobs that run a model you connect, on your key. They read your sources and open change requests for a person to review.

workflow · weekly churn notes · mondays 9:00

08

Audit log

Every change is logged with who made it and when. Admins filter the log in Settings.

audit · payout schedule · who, what, when

09

MCP

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or your own agent connects over MCP and signs in as a person. One endpoint, the same tools for every client.

app.atlascontext.ai/mcp · oauth

10

Search

Search checks access before it ranks. People and agents only find what they may open, in the browser and over MCP.

search · "refund policy" · only what you can open

11

Tool policy

Admins choose which MCP tools each role may use: everyone, admins or owners, or off. Approving a change always needs a person's explicit consent.

policy · execute_query · owners only

12

API keys

For a scheduled job with no one to sign in, an admin creates a key limited to chosen teamspaces, tables and metrics. It reads exactly that, nothing more.

key · km_live_… · finance teamspace · read
